body:
## Design session requested

Design how Render authors, stores, composes, validates, versions, and renders agent-facing prose separately from Engine implementation, including how the same overall content-handling approach can support consumer-project principles.

This is a **design investigation**, not a request to immediately extract strings, adopt Markdown or JSON, build a compiler, add a plugin system, or change the accepted `render-v1` workflow. Compare concrete alternatives, establish the intended behavior and trade-offs, and bring any consequential product or accepted-proposal changes back for human decision before implementation.

## Why this matters to Render

Render's name reflects a distinctive goal inherited from `skl`: determine the facts and workflow choices that can be known ahead of time, then **render an execution skill tailored to the particular agent run**. Instead of asking the model to reason through generic instructions and choose its own workflow, the system selects the applicable procedure, binds its real inputs and commands, and supplies the judgment guidance needed for that work.

`skl` makes the agent-visible prose a first-class thing that can be read and reviewed independently. Its authored procedures and reusable craft are separate from the Go code that selects them and supplies invocation facts. For example, Implement composes Testing and Audit; its rendered procedure varies for an initial run, resumption, or rework. See [`skl`'s agent prose model](https://github.com/vicrdguez/skills/blob/480179c/docs/agent-prose.md), [`catalog.go`](https://github.com/vicrdguez/skills/blob/480179c/catalog.go), and [`implement.md`](https://github.com/vicrdguez/skills/blob/480179c/prose/procedures/implement.md).

Render improves on that model with explicit assignment identity, durable artifacts, policy, role-specific inputs and enforced capabilities. Those improvements are valuable and must be retained. However, agent-facing prose is central to whether the remaining work is performed well. Once deterministic choices are made, the quality and clarity of the instructions and craft materially affect the outcome. Those instructions need to be easy to inspect, compare, review, test, and evolve in their own right—not merely treated as incidental strings inside runtime code.

## The gap in the current WIP

At `render-v1` proposal commit [`caa3f4b`](https://github.com/vicrdguez/render/tree/caa3f4b), the gap is concrete:

- [`Engine.render`](https://github.com/vicrdguez/render/blob/caa3f4b/src/engine/runtime.ts#L793-L947) verifies the assignment binding, loads referenced inputs and builds an assignment-specific JSON packet. The Durable integration exposes it in a `role-packet` system section. This is a real and useful rendering seam.
- That same Engine implementation conditionally assembles substantial agent-facing instruction strings for the investigation playbook, experiment work, checkpoint roles and other cases. See, for example, the [experiment instructions](https://github.com/vicrdguez/render/blob/caa3f4b/src/engine/runtime.ts#L884-L890) and [investigation instructions](https://github.com/vicrdguez/render/blob/caa3f4b/src/engine/runtime.ts#L917-L926).
- The role packet also has explicit [`instructions` and `principles` references](https://github.com/vicrdguez/render/blob/caa3f4b/src/kernel/roles.ts#L24-L36), and referenced artifacts are loaded into the packet. Thus, the problem is **not** that Render has no separate instruction artifacts; it is that important authored procedure and role prose remains coupled to the runtime implementation and lacks an equivalent, visible composition model for all the pieces.

The practical regression is that a reviewer must navigate TypeScript branches and strings to understand what a worker is told, and mentally reconstruct the applicable combination for a given assignment. Changing reusable Testing guidance or adding a procedure is harder to locate and review as a prose change. As playbooks grow, their agent-facing content risks becoming increasingly spread across scheduling and runtime code.

This is especially important because the accepted specification explicitly expects packets to include project principle statements, with relevant full principles for judgment roles, and says required material cannot be silently dropped to satisfy a token budget ([specification, packet requirements](https://github.com/vicrdguez/render/blob/caa3f4b/docs/spec.md#L588-L602)). The same specification currently calls for ordinary playbooks in code and avoids a v1 DSL or plugin system ([playbooks](https://github.com/vicrdguez/render/blob/caa3f4b/docs/spec.md#L868-L881)). The design session should assess how to improve content locality without losing that simplicity—and explicitly identify any accepted design or Contract that would need human-approved amendment rather than silently superseding it.

## Consumer-project principles are part of the same design question

A goal of Render is for consumer projects/repositories to define their own principles and have Render load the applicable material into agent work. These are project-owned guidance, distinct from Render-owned procedures and craft, but they create related needs: identify the source, resolve the selected content, retain or pin its version, include it in the appropriate assignment, and make what was supplied inspectable.

The proposal's generic retained-document and role-packet mechanisms can already carry a caller-selected principle reference. The investigation at `9f343c6` did **not** establish automatic discovery of repository principles, a principle-specific registry, semantic completeness/relevance checks, or resolution of named principle citations. A reference field alone is not the whole consumer-project feature. Check the then-current proposal when doing the design rather than assuming that finding remains unchanged.

Investigate what content-handling machinery can genuinely be shared between Render-owned prose and project-owned principles. Do **not** assume they have identical sources, selection rules, trust, meaning, or lifecycle. In particular:

- Preserve the specified inclusion of all project principle statements and relevant full principles, including principles cited by Forbidden decisions, or surface an explicit blockage/staged read as the accepted policy requires.
- Decide how a project supplies and updates its principles; how a specific assignment is tied to the relevant version; and how missing, stale, conflicting or incomplete required material is surfaced.
- Clearly distinguish accepted project guidance from unrelated repository text, source observations and evidence. Project content must not acquire authority to grant capabilities, approve Contracts, change policy, or bypass current role/assignment checks merely because it is rendered.
- Keep verification catalog data distinct from reusable Testing craft: a repository's checks and evidence expectations and Render's general testing guidance can be composed, but they are not the same kind of information.

## Questions the design should answer

### Content representation and composition

1. What are the independently authored pieces—such as procedures, playbooks, reusable craft, role guidance and project principles—and what should their interfaces and ownership be?
2. How are pieces selected and composed for an exact assignment, and how does a maintainer discover which Testing or other craft is used by a given procedure?
3. What changes when a maintainer updates reusable Testing prose, adds a procedure using existing mechanics, or adds a truly new workflow state/capability? Prose changes should not require editing Engine implementation merely to change prose; genuinely new deterministic behavior may still require code and review.
4. What is the smallest content/rendering module that improves locality without duplicating workflow policy or introducing a generic plugin system? Compare a simpler alternative and apply the deletion test.

### Storage format is open

Do **not** assume Markdown is the only or preferred storage approach. Consider, as concrete candidates, JSON (one library or multiple files), Markdown, and a structured/combined approach if warranted. Compare their readability and review diffs, composition ergonomics, validation, agent-assisted editing, packaging, and maintenance costs. Choose file boundaries for a reason rather than assuming one large file or one file per paragraph.

Separately evaluate:

- **Authoring/storage format:** what humans and authoring agents edit.
- **Internal representation:** what Render validates and composes.
- **Worker-facing format:** what the executing model actually sees.

These need not be the same: for example, JSON-authored content could render to Markdown, or JSON could remain the worker-facing format. If the worker receives identical rendered inputs and has no access to the differing source, changing storage alone does not change what it sees.

Agents can inspect and modify JSON, potentially using codemode or other available tools to parse, filter and validate it. That does **not** establish that a particular model follows JSON instructions as well as Markdown, or that every Render role has codemode. Prompt-format sensitivity varies by model and task; [this older format-comparison study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.10541) is context, not proof about Render's target agents. Decide what small, representative comparison would be useful for both authoring and actual execution rather than assuming a universal winner.

### Rendering, validation, and provenance

- Is runtime loading sufficient, or does a build-time validation/compilation step solve a concrete packaging, type-checking, versioning, or reproducibility problem? A compiler is an option, not a requirement. Generated output must not become a second hand-maintained source of truth.
- What can be checked deterministically—e.g. valid structure, references, required variables, applicable composition, missing mandatory inputs and appropriate output shape—and at what point should failures block?
- How can humans and agents preview the **actual rendered worker-facing result** for a representative or retained assignment, along with the identities/versions of its source pieces and facts? Distinguish a preview from the effective provider context where runtime composition differs.
- How are exact content versions and assignment provenance retained across continuation, recovery, policy/content changes and context refresh? Respect existing lifecycle rules; do not silently replace mandatory material or invent a new approval ceremony.
- What requires human review or behavioral evaluation rather than schema validation? Valid JSON or successful template rendering alone does not prove that the prose is clear, complete, safe, or effective.

The Engine/Kernel must remain responsible for the deterministic facts, assignment state, authorization and capability configuration. Authored prose may use small substitutions or conditionals over established facts, but should not become a second, competing workflow authority. Required content must not be silently omitted or summarized away to make it fit.

## Expected output of the design session

Produce a reviewable design, not an assumed implementation:

- Compare at least two materially different approaches and recommend one, including module seam, ownership, interface, composition, locality, validation, and reasons against the alternatives.
- Walk through concrete examples: an assignment-specific procedure, reusable Testing craft, and consumer-project principles. Show how each is authored, selected, rendered, inspected, and versioned; distinguish current functionality from proposed behavior.
- Identify the necessary decisions and changes to the existing `render-v1` specification/Contracts, if any, and which choices require the human.
- Propose focused verification and representative failure cases: missing/invalid pieces or variables, wrong composition, stale/missing project material, exact source/version selection, and agreement between rendered guidance and actual role authority. Include a way to review the real resulting prose and to assess its behavioral quality; snapshots or schema checks alone are not sufficient.
- Address how to compare relevant source/prompt formats and agent behavior without assuming one format is inherently best, and record any limits of that evidence.
- Give a scoped migration/adoption path that preserves working role packets, durable execution, existing authorization and accepted verification obligations. Avoid claiming the entire design/delivery journey is implemented today.

Related but distinct: #8 covers durable scoped agent work; #28 concerns project verification maintenance. This issue is about the **design of agent-facing content and its integration**, not a request to redefine those Slices implicitly.
title: Design first-class agent prose and project principles independently of the Engine
